Medicare for All. You’ve probably heard that phrase thrown around a lot over the last few months. My opponent has vied for this single payer “solution” to our health care system, but he accidentally slipped and said the quiet part out loud, "Medicare for All is not possible".  Our current healthcare system is broken and certainly needs to be fixed.  I think we can all agree on that.  

But while I can agree with my opponent that the current system needs fixing, there are so many issues with Medicare for All that he was actually fact checked by local media.  What they found is the very reason I disagree with his proposal:

1.  He's using outdated figures to push his ideology by saying M4A will save families $3,000 annually. 
FALSE: The AMA has never published any such study (links in comments).

2.  He references other studies that also claim monetary savings and a decrease in patient lives lost.
Both have been debunked or discredited (links in comments).

3.  While free health care for everyone sounds great, the price tag does not. The Congressional Budget Office puts the cost of Medicare for All at $1.5-$3 trillion per year (almost half of what the US spent last year). Medicare for all would increase the US spending by ~50%. 

4.  My opponent also claims that the US has the lowest life expectancy of other developed nations. However, he doesn't account for causation versus correlation. Unfortunately, heart disease, stroke, and diabetes are leading causes of death in America. Those are also medical conditions that have a proven reduced mortality rate with behavioral changes to their health choices.   While our medical system does need to be overhauled to make preventative care more accessible, Medicare for All is not a one-size-fits-all solution.

5.  According to the National Institute of Health, British studies have shown that their National Health Service (a similar version of Medicare for All) doesn’t automatically make everyone healthier. In fact, wealthier individuals were still healthier on average due to them not having sedentary life styles and the ability to use American hospitals.  

Like I've said before, it is important that we can rely on our elected officials to tell us the truth.  I encourage you to read the attached research article from The American Experiment as well as look into their linked articles.  If we're going to fix something, we have to be honest about the real problems and then come up with real, achievable solutions.

Link to article: https://www.americanexperiment.org/candidates-need-a-little-help-on-the-cost-of-medicare-for-all/
